description: Rage and betrayal is one of the three factors in the validated CTSR scale, alongside exhaustion/detachment and fear/helplessness. Inadequate response by authorities is specifically identified as what generates it.
energy_note: The anger has a domestic address.

aspect: It cannot be expressed where it would be dangerous to
description: In a state with functioning security services the anger has nowhere to go, so it turns inward or onto the family. Suppressed political rage is one of the commonest routes from war stress to domestic violence.
energy_note: Anger that can only be spent at home.

aspect: Abroad, it is misread as support for the enemy
description: The refugee who criticises their own government is assumed to endorse the people who bombed them. The refugee who does not is assumed to be a regime loyalist. There is no available position.
energy_note: Two wrong boxes and no third one.

aspect: SECONDARY - it forecloses the diaspora politics that might have helped
description: Communities fracture along these lines instead of organising, which removes the collective action that the literature identifies as the main protective factor available to people abroad.
energy_note: The one thing that helps, made impossible.
